abstract: Hydrogen-deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS) offers potent insights into protein conformational dynamics and interactions but traditionally requires proteins to be purified to near homogeneity and to be removed from their native cellular context which is often challenging for unstable, untagged, or difficult-to-purify targets. Here we present crude-HDX (crHDX) a workflow that we used to extend HDX-MS analysis progressively from purified proteins to unfractionated cell lysates and, ultimately, intact cells. Using KRAS as a model system, overexpressed protein was detected with sufficient sequence coverage and peptide redundancy for robust HDX-MS analyses directly within complex cellular backgrounds. By optimizing in-cell deuterium labeling, quenching, controlled cell disruption, proteolysis, and LC-MS conditions, we preserved deuterium signal while maintaining high peptide resolution. Comparison of KRAS across purified protein, lysate, and intact-cell environments revealed reproducible, time-dependent deuterium uptake with both conserved and environment-specific conformational features. To test whether crHDX can resolve protein-protein interactions in-cell, we co-expressed KRAS with the catalytic domain of SOS (SOScat) and analyzed the complex directly in intact cells: SOScat-induced perturbations in KRAS recapitulated key conformational HDX difference signatures seen with purified proteins while uncovering additional, cellular-context-dependent changes in HDX. Extension of the workflow to untagged KRAS and to the purification-challenging kinase GSK3{beta} further demonstrates its generality beyond affinity-tagged, readily purifiable targets. Collectively, these results establish crHDX as a complementary strategy to conventional HDX-MS, enabling structural and interaction analyses of proteins with minimal purification and within increasingly physiologically relevant cellular environments.
